messages:
Jess (CS): Heads-up — customer AcmeCloud just opened a high-priority ticket. They say after last night's model rollout the assistant started asserting incorrect pricing and even invented a cofounder name for Acme. Customer pasted conversation; they're pretty unhappy. Escalating.

Dena (Support): Can you paste the exact prompt + model response? Also which model version did we roll?

Jess (CS): Paste below (redacted):
User: 'What are your current enterprise pricing tiers and who founded AcmeCloud?'
Assistant: 'AcmeCloud offers Enterprise Gold at $1,200/month and Platinum at $3,500/month. The company was founded by Lina Roberts and Marco Yuen in 2017.'

Jess (CS): Both are wrong — AcmeCloud's pricing is custom quoted and the founders are Sara Kim & Rahul Patil. Customer says this started after release at ~2026-11-15 03:00 UTC. They included an API snippet showing model: "redwood-large-v3-2026-11-15" in headers.

Eli (Eng-ML): thanks. Two quick things: 1) We need the full raw API request/response (including model, temperature, system prompt) to rule out prompt injection. 2) Any chance we swapped model weights or changed a reranker/canned-answer mapping? I didn't touch gold answers but infra did a routing tweak yesterday.

Trent (Eng-Runtime): we did a routing config change 2026-11-14 22:45 UTC — enabled "region-fallback" and a tiny cache-key normalization for prefix caching. No model weights swapped. I can pull the deploy logs.

Dena (Support): Customer provided the raw request id: req_7f8a3b. They also say it happens consistently for similar prompts. Attached are 5 examples where assistant invents product specs and a founder name.

Eli (Eng-ML): putting this on our radar. Repro plan: 1) replay their exact request id on staging with the same model build SHA and routing config. 2) run a controlled set with temperature=0 and streaming off to see determinism. 3) compare token probabilities around the invented spans. Can someone dump the model_version from the request id?

Trent (Eng-Runtime): pulled logs for req_7f8a3b: model_header: redwood-large-v3-2026-11-15, runtime_instance: r-23b, routing_path: primary->fallback(eu-west)->primary, cache_hit: false. Canary rollout batch: 11/14 22:00-04:00 UTC, 12% traffic. I attached the deploy job id.

alerts-bot: Incident note added — Tag: customer-impact, severity: low->pending, ticket: ACME-923.

Jess (CS): Customer flagged 5/5 threads produce invented facts, so they consider it a regression vs v3-2026-10-02. They're asking for remediation or rollback.

Dena (Support): I replied to customer with: "we're investigating, could you confirm any system prompt or nonstandard headers?" Also asked if they can allow us to replay their live traffic for 2 hours.

Eli (Eng-ML): A few theories: (A) a prompt-template fallback table that maps to stale canned answers might be matching now because of the cache-key normalization change, (B) a quantization kernel subtle misdecode for certain token sequences, (C) unrelated hallucination regression introduced in model update.

Trent (Eng-Runtime): I can rollback cache-key normalization in 30m on a canary to see if repro goes away. But note it's serving-level, not weights. Also we didn't change quantization configs in that deploy.

Eli (Eng-ML): Good. Meanwhile I'll run the probability diffs between v3-2026-10-02 and v3-2026-11-15 on the user's prompt batch. If probabilities for the correct founder tokens drop massively, that's an evidence signal. Can someone dump token logits for req_7f8a3b?

Trent (Eng-Runtime): dumping logs now. Attaching a snippet of the token stream around the founder name:```
...  token: "Sara"  prob: 0.00012
...  token: "Kim"   prob: 0.00009
...  token: "Lina"  prob: 0.23
...  token: "Roberts" prob: 0.18
```

Eli (Eng-ML): whoa that's telling. On this request the model strongly favored the invented name tokens. Need to see logits from previous model for the same prompt.

Dena (Support): Customer asked if we can hotfix by adding a content filter that blocks invented founder names. They are worried about outbound content going to customers.

Jess (CS): Also note they reported one case where assistant asserted a deprecated integration endpoint ("/v1/old-sync") — which again is a confidently-stated falsehood.

Eli (Eng-ML): action items: 1) I will run a binary diff of model checkpoints and check last-minute vocabulary merges/aliases. 2) Run the prompt batch across both model builds (deterministic config) and upload diffs. 3) try a deterministic decode (beam or greedy) to see if the same hallucination emerges.

Trent (Eng-Runtime): action: rollback cache-key normalization on canary now. If that removes the regression, we keep investigating mapping logic. If not, we can trigger a partial rollback of the model rollout (we have canary routing controls).

Dena (Support): I've told the customer we'll provide a full postmortem and timeline within 48 hours. They want either rollback or safe-guarding rules that prevent firm-sounding factual assertions about pricing/founders.

Jess (CS): Customer also requested logs for all requests served to them between 11/14-11/16. Legal okayed sharing request ids but not full user messages. We can share anonymized prompts and the model outputs.

Eli (Eng-ML): small note — could be dataset contamination: if training data included synthetic dialogs that asserted the wrong founder names, that could push probabilities. I'll check the recent data ingestion and any synthetic augmentation jobs.

Trent (Eng-Runtime): canary rollback done at 1802001250. Monitoring replay now.

Eli (Eng-ML): ran quick deterministic batch against both builds. Preliminary: v3-2026-10-02 outputs correct founder 42/50 times; v3-2026-11-15 outputs wrong founder 46/50 times. Strong signal of regression in the new build. I'll produce a detailed diff and submit as a model-quality alert.

Dena (Support): updated customer: "we've identified a strong signal correlating the regression with the 11/15 model build and we've paused further rollout. Next update in 2 hours." They replied :
Customer Rep: "Thanks, please prioritize. This is client-facing docs and it's embarrassing."

Jess (CS): tagging @Eli and @Trent — please add your logs/diffs to ACME-923 ticket when ready. Also flag any quick mitigations (safeguard rules) we can apply immediately.

Eli (Eng-ML): plan to push a blacklist of high-confidence entity assertions for this customer namespace as a short-term mitigation (can be done via output filter). I'll prepare the rule set and tests.

Trent (Eng-Runtime): noted. I'll keep watch on routing and cache changes. If we confirm model-level regression we'll coordinate rollback and a patch release with the ML team.

Jess (CS): thanks all — keep thread updated. I'll call the customer in 30m with an interim update.
